segments.card:
THE COURT OF
MUSICAL APPEALS

docket 145
segments.say: The Court of Musical Appeals is now in session. Docket one four five. The league versus Conor Johnston.
segments.style: Court clerk calling a room to order. Formal, bored, institutional.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
Mr. Johnston. You are the author
of this document, are you not?
segments.say: Mr. Johnston. You are the author of this document, are you not?
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel beginning a cross-examination. Silky, patient, absolutely certain of the answer.

segments.card:
>>"This competition is one big joke to you, eh?
>>A gag for you to poop on? The rest of us put
>>thought into this, effort. And you come here
>>why? To mock us for caring?"
segments.say: This competition is one big joke to you, eh? A gag for you to poop on? The rest of us put thought into this, effort. And you come here why? To mock us for caring?
segments.style: Counsel reading a damning document aloud into the record, with quiet relish.

segments.card: WITNESS:
segments.say: Yes... sir.
segments.style: A timid, reedy Englishman in a witness box. Cornered. Voice tight and higher than natural, trailing off. He knows exactly where this is going.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
And you wrote it about a man
in his first round
in this league.
segments.say: And you wrote it about a man in his very first round in this league.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel. Not a question. Flat, devastating.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
And you agree that on that same
evening, on that same ballot,
you submitted this.
segments.say: And you agree that on that same evening, on that same ballot, you yourself submitted this.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel producing an exhibit.

segments.card:
Andrea Bocelli — “Con Te Partirò”
submitted by Conor Johnston

COUNSEL: ...which, by your own
description, you could not identify.

>>"I have no idea to this day what those 2
>>Italian ladies were signing about.
>>Truth is, I don't want to know."
segments.say: I have no idea to this day what those two Italian ladies were singing about. Truth is, I don't want to know.
segments.style: Counsel reading the defendant's own words back at him, slowly.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
There is one singer.
He is a man.
segments.say: There is one singer, Mr. Johnston. He is a man.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel delivering a small, lethal correction.

segments.card: WITNESS:
segments.say: Yes... sir.
segments.style: Timid reedy Englishman, thoroughly beaten now, almost a whisper.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
And the theme that week was —
read it to the court.
segments.say: And the theme that week was — read it to the court.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel, closing the trap.

segments.card:
“Songs must contain vocals
entirely or mostly in a language
other than English.”
segments.say: Songs must contain vocals entirely or mostly in a language other than English.
segments.style: A timid Englishman reading his own indictment aloud, getting quieter with every word.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
And you agree that everyone hated
your song — and by inference,
your very presence.
segments.say: And you agree that everyone hated your song. And by inference, your very presence.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel. Cruel, calm, enjoying it.

segments.card: WITNESS:
segments.say: Yes... sir.
segments.style: Timid reedy Englishman. Utterly defeated. Barely audible.

board: 7.  Grupo Soñador — El Paso Del Gigante
segments.card: ROUND 145 — FINAL
segments.say: Let the record show the final standings.
segments.style: Court clerk entering a document into the record.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
You finished beneath
the man you called ignorant.
segments.say: You finished beneath the man you called ignorant.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel. Silky, patient, entirely in control.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
But the court needn't
take my word for it.
segments.say: But the court needn't take my word for it.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel. Silky, patient, entirely in control.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
Mr. Johnston — would you read
aloud, for the record, your own
comment of August the first?
segments.say: Mr. Johnston. Would you read aloud, for the record, your own comment of August the first?
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel. Silky, patient, entirely in control.

segments.card:
>>"I went pretty hard after Tequila.
>>Then it beat me. Soooo...I should keep
>>my lard ass mouth closed."

— Conor Johnston, group chat, August 1
segments.say: I went pretty hard after Tequila. Then it beat me. Soooo. I should keep my lard ass mouth closed.
segments.style: Timid, reedy Englishman in a witness box. Utterly beaten. Reading his own words aloud, quietly, hating every syllable.

segments.card:
COUNSEL:
I rest my case,
your honor.
segments.say: I rest my case, your honor.
segments.style: Prosecuting counsel sitting down. Quiet, final, deeply satisfied.

segments.card:
THE COURT:
For the offense of excessive
and wholly unearned sanctimony —

the court finds the defendant —
segments.say: For the offense of excessive and wholly unearned sanctimony, the court finds the defendant —
segments.style: A weary judge delivering a verdict. Building, then cutting off hard on the last word.

segments.card: GUILTY
